name: OH-06
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+17 district fundamentals with incumbent Michael Rulli running again
Massive fundraising gap: Rulli $1.4M raised vs. Kirtley ~$10K
Prediction markets price Rulli at about 97 percent
No public polls or expert ratings indicate a competitive race
model.rationale: A deeply Republican district, a roughly 140-to-1 fundraising advantage for Rulli, and markets pricing his win odds near 97 percent all point the same way, and even the favorable national environment for Democrats falls far short of what Kirtley would need.
model.watch: Any public polling showing Kirtley within single digits or significant outside spending entering the district would be the first sign the race is actually in play.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Ohio's 6th District leans heavily Republican, and first-term incumbent Michael Rulli is seeking a second term after winning the seat in 2024. Democrat Elizabeth Kirtley has run a minimal campaign, raising about $10,000 with under $5,000 on hand, while Rulli has brought in roughly $1.4 million and holds more than $460,000 in cash. No public general-election polls are available, and prediction markets give Rulli about a 97 percent chance of winning.

The district's R+17 fundamentals, the incumbent's financial dominance, and the absence of outside spending or expert attention all point the same direction. Even a strong national Democratic environment would need to swing this district by well over ten points to put Kirtley in contention. The race is rated a heavy favorite for Rulli, with the main uncertainty coming from the lack of polling rather than any evidence of an actual contest.
